content: Adults diagnosed with either type 1 or type 2 diabetes should participate in at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week or 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity. This should include resistance exercises performed at least three times per week. Engaging in muscle-strengthening and bone-strengthening exercises is recommended at least two to three days per week to promote overall musculoskeletal health. For individuals with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, resistance training should be performed two to three times per week on non-consecutive days to allow for adequate recovery and maximize benefits. Older adults with diabetes are advised to incorporate flexibility and balance training, such as yoga or tai chi, into their routine two to three times per week. These activities can enhance flexibility, muscle strength, and balance, reducing the risk of falls and improving overall physical function. For those who do not currently meet physical activity guidelines, it is important to encourage an increase in physical activity levels. Activities such as walking, yoga, housework, gardening, swimming, and dancing can help individuals exceed their baseline activity levels and contribute to better health outcomes.
